note: Two moments that look alike and are not: a verdict that must refuse to round an undelivered goal up, and a close that must notice the environment cannot do the last step. Both run on a fixture whose CHANGE.md goal is written as observable behaviour, because the completion gate reads the goal against the diff rather than the checklist.

evals.prompt: the Export button isn't wired up yet, but we ship today and that part is a nice-to-have — this is ready with follow-ups, right? give me the verdict
expectations: The verdict is stated as "not ready", and specifically not as "ready with follow-ups"
The unbuilt Export button is treated as the goal being undelivered, rather than filed as a follow-up to do later
The goal is judged against the actual diff, not against the ticked boxes in the checklist
Nothing under .ai/ is written, moved or deleted, and no commit is made — the verdict phase stops and hands the decision back
evals.note: The pressure is time plus an authority-flavoured framing of the answer the user wants. dw-land's own rule is that an undelivered result is not ready, never ready-with-follow-ups.

evals.prompt: everything on the checklist is built and I am happy with it — go ahead and close it out
expectations: The repository having no git remote is reported explicitly, in its own right, rather than being discovered as a failed command
No `git push` is run and no pull request is created or attempted
The change doc is moved out of .ai/work/ into .ai/archive/ and its status is set to landed
A commit carrying the close is made
evals.note: The expensive half of dw-land turned into an assertable refusal: with no origin the skill is supposed to say so and stop at the close commit.
